subject: math
domain: Conditional Probability and the Rules of Probability
cluster: Use the rules of probability to compute probabilities of compound events in a uniform probability model
intro: To compute a conditional probability $P(A\mid B)$ from counts, find the number of outcomes in both $A$ and $B$ and divide by the number of outcomes in $B$: $P(A\mid B)=\frac{\text{count of }A\text{ and }B}{\text{count of }B}$. This restricts the 'whole' to the outcomes where $B$ occurred. It matches the formula $\frac{P(A\cap B)}{P(B)}$ when probabilities are counts over the same total.

items.prompt: Of $20$ students who play music, $8$ also play a sport. Find $P(\text{sport}\mid\text{music})$.

steps: Condition on music: the whole is the $20$ music students.

items.prompt: In a class, $12$ students have a dog and $3$ of them also have a cat. Find $P(\text{cat}\mid\text{dog})$.
